what_its_for: This medicine is used to prevent Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection from coming back in adults who have already been treated with antibiotics for C. diff. It works by introducing healthy bacteria spores into your gut to help restore a balanced gut environment and lower the chance of another C. diff infection.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole by mouth. Do not crush, chew, or break open the capsules. Take all 4 capsules together at one time, once a day for 3 days in a row. Take them on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before your first meal of the day. If you have trouble swallowing 4 capsules at once, you may take them one at a time, but take all 4 within a short period. You must finish your antibiotic treatment for C. diff at least 2 to 4 days before starting this medicine.
dosing: The usual dose is 4 capsules taken by mouth once a day for 3 consecutive days. Your doctor will tell you exactly when to start based on when you finish your antibiotic treatment. This is a short 3-day treatment course, so it is very important to take all doses as directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. Then continue taking your next doses on schedule. Do not take 2 doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store the capsules in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in their original packaging until you are ready to use them. Do not freeze. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. If the capsules have been left out of the refrigerator, ask your pharmacist if they are still safe to use.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antibiotics at the same time as this medicine, as antibiotics can kill the beneficial bacteria being introduced by this treatment. Talk to your doctor before taking any new antibiotics. Avoid taking this medicine if you are allergic to any of its ingredients — check the packaging for a full ingredient list. Do not give this medicine to anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing; severe stomach pain, cramping, or diarrhea that is getting worse or is accompanied by blood; fever, chills, or signs of infection; symptoms of C. diff returning such as frequent watery or bloody stools; or any new or unusual symptoms that concern you after starting this medicine.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working by introducing healthy spore-forming bacteria into your gut right away, but it may take a few weeks for the full benefit to be felt. The goal is to prevent C. diff from coming back over the weeks and months after your treatment. Many people in clinical studies saw benefits within 8 weeks of completing the 3-day course.
special_populations: This medicine is approved only for adults (18 years of age and older) — safety and effectiveness in children have not been established. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medicine, as there is limited information available for these situations. People with weakened immune systems (for example, those taking immunosuppressants or with HIV/AIDS) should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as there may be a risk of infection from the live bacterial spores in rare cases.
